question: To what amount did SBP raise the regulatory retail portfolio limit under the Basel framework in 2024, and from what previous limit?
reference: BPRD Circular No. 04 of 2024 (October 7, 2024) raised the regulatory retail portfolio limit from PKR 180 million to PKR 300 million with immediate effect.

question: Which earlier circular on Minimum Capital Requirements does BPRD Circular No. 04 of 2024 refer to?
reference: It refers to BSD Circular No. 5 of 2008 on Minimum Capital Requirements (and BPRD Circular Letter No. 12 of 2020 on COVID-19 regulatory relief).

question: From which date is the Minimum Profit Rate requirement no longer applicable to deposits of financial institutions, public sector enterprises and public limited companies?
reference: From January 01, 2025, per BPRD Circular No. 05 of 2024.

question: Which types of depositors are excluded from the minimum rate of return on saving deposits requirement under BPRD Circular No. 05 of 2024?
reference: Deposits of financial institutions, public sector enterprises and public limited companies are excluded from the Minimum Profit Rate requirement.

question: For how many consecutive years must an NPL be classified as 'Loss' before a bank may charge it off?
reference: The NPL must have remained in the 'Loss' category, fully provided, for at least five consecutive years (BPRD Circular No. 02 of 2024).

question: What condition applies to charging off NPLs above PKR 10 million?
reference: For NPLs exceeding PKR 10 million, the bank must have filed a recovery suit at least two years before the charge-off.

question: Which borrowers' NPLs are NOT eligible for charge-off under BPRD Circular No. 02 of 2024?
reference: NPLs of related parties, sponsor shareholders, directors, executives or politically exposed persons, and NPLs under criminal litigation, cannot be charged off.

question: Does charging off a loan give the borrower financial relief?
reference: No. Charge-offs do not constitute any financial relief; the bank's right to recover from the borrower remains intact and the loan continues to be reported to e-CIB/credit bureaus as overdue.

question: How must banks disclose charged-off loans?
reference: Banks must disclose charged-off loans under a separate note in their financial statements, using the format in Annexure A of BPRD Circular No. 02 of 2024, and maintain proper records of them.

question: Within what time frame must banks develop and implement an NPLs Management Strategy?
reference: Within six months from the issuance of BPRD Circular No. 03 of 2024 (dated July 22, 2024), with the strategy approved by the Board of Directors.

question: How often must a bank's NPL Management Strategy be reviewed at a minimum?
reference: At least once in three years, or earlier in case of any material change.

question: What time horizons do the NPL guidelines define for short-, medium- and long-term NPL reduction targets?
reference: Short-term: one year; medium-term: up to three years; long-term: over three years.

question: How frequently should the Board review the movement and recovery status of charged-off loans according to the NPL management guidelines?
reference: At least quarterly.

question: List the implementation options the NPL Management Strategy guidelines mention for resolving NPLs.
reference: Restructuring/rescheduling; portfolio reduction via sale, transfer or assignment to Corporate Restructuring Companies; write-offs of irrecoverable loans; debt-to-equity swaps; debt-to-asset swaps; collateral substitution; and legal options (court proceedings and out-of-court settlements).

question: To whom should internal audit report its findings on implementation of the NPL strategy?
reference: To the Board Audit Committee (BAC).

question: When a bank transfers NPAs to a Corporate Restructuring Company, what share of the provision may be reversed to profit and loss immediately?
reference: Up to 10% of the fair value of the financial instruments received; the remaining 90% is recognised only on cash receipt or redemption. The 10% is not available for dividends.

question: Over how many years, and in what annual percentages, may a bank phase the recognition of a loss on NPAs transferred to a CRC below net book value?
reference: Over a maximum of five years: 10% in year 1, 15% in year 2, 20% in year 3, 25% in year 4 and 30% in year 5.

question: What risk weight applies to financial instruments received from a CRC as consideration for NPAs?
reference: A risk weight of 50 percent, or as per applicable Basel instructions, whichever is lower.

question: What are the two engagement models with a CRC described in the revised guidelines?
reference: (1) True transfer and assignment on a non-recourse basis with all risks and rewards transferred and the NPA derecognised; (2) an agency agreement under Section 6B of the Act, where the CRC acts as recovery agent and the NPAs stay on the bank's books.

question: Which earlier circular letter did the revised CRC guidelines of 2024 replace?
reference: BPRD Circular Letter No. 40 of 2020.

question: Until when may financial institutions continue to measure unquoted equity securities at the lower of cost or break-up value under the IFRS 9 amendments?
reference: Until December 31, 2024; from January 1, 2025 they must be measured at fair value.

question: From what date must banks apply the effective interest rate (EIR) method for recognising interest income and expense under IFRS 9?
reference: From October 1, 2024 (existing practices were permitted until September 30, 2024).

question: What extension was given for developing Exposure at Default (EAD) models for revolving products?
reference: An extension until December 31, 2024 for developing models to calculate EAD for revolving products beyond contractual maturity.

question: What minimum CCTV camera resolution did SBP prescribe in October 2024, and how does it compare with the earlier requirement?
reference: At least five (5) megapixels, reduced from the earlier requirement of at least six (6) megapixels in BPRD Circular Letter No. 31 of 2022.

question: By what date must banks install the prescribed CCTV cameras at critical points of branches in Tier-1 cities and high-risk geographies?
reference: By March 31, 2025.

question: What was the temporary change to the biometric verification requirement for Asaan Mobile Accounts in 2024?
reference: Instead of biometric verification within 60 days of account opening, banks/MFBs may conduct Call Back Confirmation (CBC) within 30 days of opening the AMA (BPRD Circular Letter No. 07 of 2024, March 28, 2024).

question: What new disclosure was added to the format of annual financial statements of banks and DFIs in 2024, and from which accounting year does it apply?
reference: A disclosure of advances to women and women-owned/managed enterprises (sub-notes 9.2.1 and 9.2.2 of Note 9 'Advances'), effective from the accounting year ending December 31, 2024.

question: What were the banking hours for the public on Fridays during Ramadan 1445 AH?
reference: 08:30 a.m. to 01:00 p.m. without break (Monday-Thursday: 09:00 a.m. to 02:00 p.m. without break).

question: Which circular on the clean note policy was withdrawn in November 2024?
reference: BPRD Circular No. 01 of 2010 dated January 05, 2010 was withdrawn with immediate effect by BPRD Circular Letter No. 22 of 2024; other SBP instructions on the subject remain applicable.

question: Who bears the cost of opening BISP Sahulat accounts and issuing ATM cards to beneficiaries?
reference: Banks recover all upfront and ongoing costs from BISP; no charges may be levied on BISP beneficiaries.
